papers.title_en: StereoDiffuer: Diffusion-based Progressive Geometry Modeling with Saliency Attention Perception for Stereo Matching
papers.evidence: 基于扩散的迭代立体匹配，保持边界与薄结构等几何细节
papers.tldr: 现有立体匹配方法在挑战区域常丢失细粒度几何细节，导致边缘模糊和过度平滑。为此提出StereoDiffuer，一种基于迭代扩散的立体匹配框架，通过Saliency Attention Perception模块提取边界、薄结构等显著线索，并结合置信度引导去噪过程逐步修正视差误差。在Scene Flow和KITTI基准上验证了方法的有效性，获得具有竞争力的性能。该工作展示了扩散模型用于几何细节恢复的潜力，为立体匹配提供了新思路。
papers.abstract_en: With the advance of deep neural networks, the quality of disparity maps obtained through stereo matching has steadily improved. However, existing stereo matching methods still struggle to preserve fine-grained geometric details, resulting in blurred edges and over-smoothed predictions in challenging regions. To address these limitations, we propose StereoDiffuer, an iterative diffusion-based stereo matching framework that explicitly models geometric details and progressively refines disparity estimates. The framework incorporates a Saliency Attention Perception (SAP) module to extract salient geometric cues, including object boundaries, thin structures, and sharp edges. Confidence-guided SAP features are combined with the initial disparity estimate to condition an iterative denoising diffusion process, which corrects residual disparity errors and restores geometric details suppressed during cost-volume regularization and upsampling. Experimental results on the Scene Flow and KITTI benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework and its competitive performance relative to the compared stereo matching methods.

papers.title_en: Steer the Sampling, Not the Kernel Grid: Geometry-Guided Sampling Operator for Volumetric Segmentation
papers.authors: Sizhe Wang, Himashi Peiris, Zhaolin Chen
papers.evidence: 面向血管等细长结构的几何引导采样分割算子，可迁移到发丝边界处理
papers.tldr: 三维分割中细长结构（如血管）易因边界误差导致拓扑错误，而传统编码器-解码器网络的重复下采样与固定网格卷积会模糊细节。为此，提出几何引导的采样算子，在每一体素预测局部方向与步长，沿方向对称采样并生成几何与边界线索，同时通过跨尺度一致性对齐跳跃连接特征。在BraTS、MSD肝血管和TDSC-ABUS上，该方法显著提升边界指标（如BraTS HD95从7.1降至6.2），参数由2.3M降至0.8M。该算子可无缝集成至nnU-Net、Swin-UNETR等骨干，无需改动宏观架构即带来稳定增益。
papers.abstract_en: Accurate 3D segmentation is central to quantitative lesion assessment and anatomy mapping for clinical planning and follow-up. Thin, elongated, and fine anatomical/pathological structures (e.g., vessels) are a particularly challenging case: a one-voxel boundary error can disconnect a branch and change clinically relevant topology. In encoder-decoder networks (e.g., U-Net), repeated downsampling and fixed-grid convolution blur or alias fine structures and weaken orientation cues, so early mistakes propagate across scales. We propose a geometry-guided local operator that steers where features are sampled, rather than deforming convolutional kernels, under a single formulation for both feature refinement (stride 1) and resolution reduction (stride > 1). At each voxel, it predicts a local orientation and bounded step sizes, samples symmetrically along these directions, and transforms paired samples into compact geometric and boundary cues with lightweight mixing; a cross-scale consensus aligns encoder and decoder features at skip connections to reduce geometric mismatch. Replacing all stride 1 and stride 2 operators in a 3D U-Net yields consistent improvements on BraTS, MSD Hepatic Vessel, and TDSC-ABUS, with notably better boundary metrics (e.g., BraTS Dice 86.1 to 88.9, HD95 7.1 to 6.2; TDSC-ABUS HD95 39.1 to 27.8) while reducing parameters from 2.3M to 0.8M. We further demonstrate that the operator can be integrated into other backbones (e.g., nnU-Net, Swin-UNETR, and MedNeXt) without changing their macro-architectures while providing consistent performance gains.

papers.title_en: VisTa3D: A Dataset and Benchmark for Thin Object Reconstruction from Vision, Tactile, and 3D Point Clouds
papers.authors: Shania Guo, Yeongsik Seo, Andrew Fu, Mei Hao, Iris Xia, Jiwon Jenny Lee, Xinyi Mary Xie, Hyoungseob Park, Aaron Dollar, Alex Wong
papers.evidence: 薄物体深度与分割数据集，针对薄结构深度估计难题
papers.tldr: 现有3D重建模型在薄物体上表现不佳，因为薄物体在图像和点云中占据空间很小。为此，构建了首个薄物体重建数据集VisTa3D，包含同步RGB、深度、触觉响应图以及相机位姿、惯性测量和激光扫描真值。基于387个场景、70种薄物体和17种环境，评测了多个现有模型，确认其保真度较低。进一步提出融合视觉、距离和触觉的3D重建基线，证明触觉信息有助于薄物体重建，并公开数据与代码。
papers.abstract_en: State-of-the-art 3D reconstruction models, whether from visual, range, or both, tend to underperform on thin objects. This is partially due to the small amount of space such objects occupy in RGB images and in 3D point clouds. To test the extent of their errors, we collected the first thin object dataset comprising of synchronized RGB images, depth maps, and tactile response maps, where each frame is associated with inertial measurements, camera pose and calibration, and groundtruth depth and segmentation maps obtained from laser scanning of thin objects. We hypothesize that tactile data can aid in the reconstruction of thin objects as their response maps provide local shape and deformation information. Our dataset, termed VisTa3D, comprises of 387 scenes covering 70 thin objects over 17 environments. We benchmarked current 3D reconstruction models on VisTa3D and found that, indeed, they exhibit low fidelity on thin objects. To test if tactile data can help, we introduce the first visual-range-tactile 3D reconstruction model as a baseline. Code and data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/shaniaguo/VisTa3D.
